title: Sandbox Runtime policy v1
description: The complete effective policy supplied by a trusted caller. Schema validation checks document structure, not runtime feasibility or isolation.
$comment: Runtime parsing additionally limits the original UTF-8 document to 65536 bytes, rejects duplicate object keys, trailing documents, unpaired Unicode surrogates and nonliteral version tokens such as 1.0/1e0. Runtime filesystem checks and backend capability checks are mandatory; see README.md.

version.description: Wire representation must be the integer token 1.

read.description: Retain the host user's read access, except the explicit denyRead rules. This is not a workspace read allowlist.

denyRead.description: Deny content access and modification. Omission means an empty list.

allowWrite.description: Grant writes to these paths subject to all denials. Omission means an empty list.

denyWrite.description: Write denials override a broader allowWrite ancestor. An allowWrite at or beneath a denial is rejected. Omission means an empty list.

temp.description: private allocates a unique writable directory per run; it does not provide cross-task confidentiality under host-read.

hostUnixSockets.description: Host named Unix socket endpoints remain forbidden in both network modes.

inherit.description: Select validated host values. PATH is always the fixed system path, even when omitted. Omission means no other host values are selected. Arbitrary environment overrides are unsupported.

rules.$comment: Runtime also rejects equivalent rules expressed through symlink, case-insensitive, or other filesystem aliases. No separate rule-count quota is imposed beyond the document byte limit.

path.description: An existing absolute Unix literal path, with no control characters, glob syntax, or dot/dot-dot components. Runtime verifies file kind, resolves symlinks and checks filesystem identities. The entire encoded policy must fit within 65536 bytes.

scope.description: file requires a regular file; tree requires a directory and applies to that object and its descendants.
